FACULTY SENATE OFFICE FACULTY SENATE LEGISLATION MARCH 28, 2024 Curriculum & Standards Committee Report 2023-2024-07A At the March 7, 2024 meeting of the Curriculum & Standards Committee, the following matters were considered and are now presented to the Faculty Senate for approval. SECTION I Informational Matters TEMPORARY COURSES COLLEGE OF THE ENVIRONMENT AND LIFE SCIENCES: GEO 222X | Earthquakes and Volcanoes, Effective Spring 2025 Temporary Course (3 crs.) Introduction to the physical and chemical nature of Earthquake and Volcanoes. Monitoring, measurements, hazards, historical and societal impacts and will be discussed, along with the theory of Plate Tectonics (Lec. 3) Pre: 100-level GEO or OCG course or equivalent; or by permission of instructor COLLEGE OF BUSINESS: ACC 301 | Intermediate Accounting I, Effective Fall 2024 Create online version of existing course (3 crs.) Valuation, recognition and disclosure relative to current and long-term assets and revenue recognition. (Lec. 3/Online) Pre: ACC (BUS) 201 or 201H or permission of instructor. May be repeated once.

SECTION II Curricular Matters Which Require Confirmation By The Faculty Senate COURSE CHANGES COLLEGE OF ARTS & SCIENCES: AAF 300 | Special Topics in African and Afro-American Studies, Effective Fall 2024 Change prerequisites (3 crs.) Selected contemporary topics, problems, issues, and individuals from the field of African and Afro- American studies.
The topical format allows in-depth analysis of some significant aspect of the African and Afro-American experience. (Lec. 3/Online) Topic: Conditions for Community Service is service learning.
Pre: AAF 201 or 202 or permission of instructor.
Some topics may be offered online.
May be repeated with different topic.
CSC 211 | Computer Programming, Effective Fall 2024 Modify prerequisites to be more specific (4 crs.) Problem specification, solution design, and algorithm development.
Topics may include data types, functions, iteration, recursion, object-oriented programming, built-in data structures, file operations, numerical and string-based operations. (Lec. 3, Lab. 2) Pre: (C- or better in CSC 110) or (B or better in (CSC 106 or CSC 201 or CSC 200) and concurrent enrollment in CSC 110) or ELE 208 or permission of instructor.

JOR 310 | News Media Law and Ethics, Effective Fall 2024 Change description, prerequisites, add content from deleted course JOR 410 (3 crs.) Examines role of the law in news media, including freedom of the press, journalists' privileges and responsibilities, libel, privacy and others.
Explores philosophical basis for ethical decision making in journalism. (Lec. 3) Pre: junior standing and 110 and one 300-level journalism skills course or permission of instructor.
MUS 110C | Applied Music – Keyboard, Effective Fall 2024 Change instrument from Organ to Keyboard (1-2 crs.) Private instruction in performance for general students.
One credit equals a weekly half-hour lesson; two credits equal weekly hour lesson.
Not for music majors or minors.
Audition and jury required. (Studio) Pre: audition and permission of chairperson.
May be repeated for credit.
MUS 110D | Applied Music – Amplified Voice, Effective Fall 2024 Change instrument from Harpsichord to Amplified Voice (1-2 crs.) Private instruction in performance for general students.
One credit equals a weekly half-hour lesson; two credits equal weekly hour lesson.
Not for music majors or minors.

Audition and jury required. (Studio) Pre: audition and permission of chairperson.
May be repeated for credit.
MUS 210D | Applied Music – Amplified Voice, Effective Fall 2024 Change instrument from Harpsichord to Amplified Voice (1-2 crs.) Private instruction in performance for music majors and minors.
Juries required.
One credit equals weekly half-hour lesson; two credits equal weekly hour lesson with music convocation performance. (Studio) Pre: Pre: audition and permission of chairperson.
May be repeated for credit.

MUS 410C | Applied Music – Organ, Effective Fall 2024 Delete course (2 crs.) Upper-level private instruction in performance for music majors.
One-hour weekly studio lessons require additional preparation and tasks as well as higher levels of performance including music convocation and/or recital.
Juries required. (Studio) Pre: MUS 210 (8 credits) and successful passage of Advancement Jury.
May be repeated for credit.
Not for graduate credit, except MUS 410V (Composition).
MUS 410D | Applied Music – Amplified Voice, Effective Fall 2024 Change instrument from Harpsichord to Amplified Voice (2 crs.) Upper-level private instruction in performance for music majors.
One-hour weekly studio lessons require additional preparation and tasks as well as higher levels of performance including music convocation and/or recital.
Juries required. (Studio) Pre: MUS 210 (8 credits) and successful passage of Advancement Jury.
May be repeated for credit.
Not for graduate credit, except MUS 410V (Composition).
MUS 445 | Vocal Pedagogy, Effective Fall 2024 Change credits (2 crs.) In-depth study of how singing tone is produced, accompanied by practical applications in supervised studio teaching experiences.

Additional topics to include voice issues in the 21st century singing community. (Lec. 2) Pre: MUS 173, 235, 442 and concurrent enrollment in MUS 410 and permission of instructor.
Not for graduate credit.
WRT 404 | Writing with Community Partners, Effective Fall 2024 Remove prerequisite and reference to old course code in description (4 crs.) Study and practice of writing with community partners.
Involves community service outside class, research, writing, and design.
May include grant proposals, brochures, websites, or reports.
Requires sustained fieldwork. (Seminar 3, Practicum 2) Not for graduate credit.
COLLEGE OF BUSINESS: TMD 203 | Textile Science, Effective Fall 2024 Change course number from 303 to 203 (3 crs.) The primary textile industry: fiber to finished fabric.
Textile fibers and their properties; yarns, fabric construction, dyeing, finishing, and printing. (Lec. 3) Pre: TM or TMD majors admitted to the College of Business and credit in CHM 105.
Concurrent enrollment in TMD 213.

TMD 213 | Textile Science Laboratory, Effective Fall 2024 Change course number from 313 to 213 (1 cr.) Laboratory exercises in fiber identification, fabric analysis and fabric performance testing, dyeing and finishing. (Lab. 2 ) Pre: Students must be admitted to the degree-granting college of BUS as TM or TM majors, and enrolled in TMD 203.
TMD 346 | Computer-Aided Textile and Apparel Design, Effective Fall 2024 Delete course (3 crs.) Development and production of textile and apparel designs and patterns using selected computer software packages.
Implications for use in the apparel industry. (Lec. 1, Lab 4/Online) Pre: Pre: TMD 126 or permission of instructor.

COLLEGE OF ENGINEERING: OCE 495 | Ocean Systems Design Project I, Effective Fall 2024 Add prerequisites (3 crs.) Capstone design of an ocean system under the direction of a faculty advisor.
Project must include engineering, economic, environmental, safety, and societal considerations.
This is first of a two-course ocean engineering design sequence. (Lec. 3) Pre: OCE 394, OCE 408, OCE 471, or permission of instructor.
Not for graduate credit.
COLLEGE OF HEALTH SCIENCES: HLT 360 | Health Services Administration, Effective Fall 2024 Change prerequisites (3 crs.) Introduction to key concepts and principles in health services administration through both didactic and experiential means. (Seminar/Online) Pre: junior standing, Public Health majors only, or permission of instructor.
KIN 122 | Human Anatomy and Physiology, Effective Fall 2024 Change prerequisites (4 crs.) Structure and function of organ systems of the human body with emphasis on applications to human health. (Lec. 3, Online 1/Online) Pre: Not for major credit in BA Biology or BS Biological Sciences.
Not open to Kinesiology majors.

KIN 370 | Kinesiology, Effective Fall 2024 Change prerequisites (3 crs.) The study of human movement based on anatomical, physiological, and mechanical principles.
Emphasis on application of these principles to fundamental movement and physical education activity. (Lec. 3) Pre: Kinesiology major; BIO 220 and 221; or permission of instructor.
COLLEGE OF PHARMACY: BPS 422 | Endocrine, Gastrointestinal, and Biotechnologic Drugs, Effective Fall 2024 Delete course (2 crs.) Mechanisms of action of drugs used to treat endocrine and gastrointestinal disorders.
Biological and biotechnologic sources, isolation, design, and medicinal chemistry of biopolymer drugs. (Lec. 2) Pre: second- year Doctor of Pharmacy student in good standing; or permission of the instructor.
BPS 410 | Foundations for Human Disease V: GI, Endocrine, Effective Fall 2024 Delete course (2 crs.) Cross-listed as (PHP), BPS 410.
The etiology, pathogenesis, symptomatology, and diagnosis of endocrine, and gastrointestinal diseases. (Lec. 2) Pre: P3 standing in the Doctor of Pharmacy program.
PHP 410 | Foundations for Human Disease V: GI, Endocrine, Effective Fall 2024 Delete course (2 crs.) Cross-listed as (PHP), BPS 410.
The etiology, pathogenesis, symptomatology, and diagnosis of endocrine, and gastrointestinal diseases. (Lec. 2) Pre: P3 standing in the Doctor of Pharmacy program.

PHP 414 | Pharmacotherapy of Gastrointestinal and Endocrine Diseases, Effective Fall 2024 Delete course (3 crs.) The appropriate use of medications in the treatment of human disease.
Interpretation of clinical data to design, monitor, and modify drug therapy in endocrine and gastrointestinal disease. (Lec. 3) Pre: second- year Doctor of Pharmacy student in good standing; or permission of the instructor.
NEW COURSES COLLEGE OF ARTS & SCIENCES: APG 370 | Decolonial Ecologies, Effective Fall 2024 (3 crs.) Examines Afro-descendant and Indigenous lives, cultural ecology, local ecological knowledge, environmental justice, and initiatives and organizing efforts to resist on-going threats to coastal livelihoods throughout the Americas. (Seminar) Pre: Sophomore standing and APG 200 or APG 203; or permission of instructor CCJ 285 | Introduction to the Courts and Criminal Procedure, Effective Fall 2024 (3 crs.) Examines the origins and development of the current criminal court system in the US.

Legal practices, procedures, and alternatives both traditional and novel will also be explored. (Lec. 3/Online) Pre: CCJ majors who have earned a C or better in CCJ/PSC 274(H), or by permission of instructor.
COM 204 | Introduction to Sports Broadcasting, Effective Fall 2024 (3 crs.) The study & practice of sports broadcasting with emphasis on producing sports feature reports, play- by-play & analyst production for television and radio, production of sports radio talk shows, and anchoring television sportscasts. (Lec. 3/Online) Pre: COM 100, and declared major or minor in Sports Media and Communication.
COLLEGE OF HEALTH SCIENCES: NUT 496 | Applied Research in Nutrition, Effective Fall 2024 (1-3 crs.) Literature review, laboratory work, and/or individual research under the direction of an associated faculty member. (Independent Study) Pre: By permission of instructor.
Not for graduate credit.
NUT 497 | Advanced Applied Nutrition Practicum, Effective Fall 2024 (1-3 crs.) Act as a peer education assistant for students enrolled in advanced nutrition courses to gain experience in team building, application of nutrition knowledge, and mentorship of students enrolled in NUT 495.

May be repeated for up to 6 credits. (Practicum) Pre: NUT 495 or by permission of instructor.
Not for graduate credit.

Describe the change you are proposing.
This organization change will bring the Public Relations B.A. program, which is currently housed in the Communication Studies department, and the Journalism B.A. program together in a new Journalism and Public Relations department. 2.
Give the rationale for your proposed change.
In 1997, the B.A. in Public Relations was approved as an interdepartmental program jointly run by the Communication Studies department and the Journalism department.

The original legislation (Bill #96- 97-26) called for the program to be administered on a “three-year rotating basis by the Chairs of Journalism and Communication Studies” with an “advisory/admissions committee” comprised of both chairs from the respective departments and the faculty who taught in the program.
Somewhere in the twenty-five plus years that have elapsed since the original proposal, the Public Relations program was effectively subsumed by Communication Studies and the interdepartmental structure of the original vision was lost.
During the academic program review of Journalism this past year, external reviewers suggested the Journalism curriculum would benefit from a “rethinking of [Harrington’s] overall department structure.” While it was originally proposed that the department might merge with the program in Sports Media Communication, subsequent conversations with faculty suggested that public relations would be a better fit as this pairing is common in institutions across the country and presents additional opportunities for collaboration due to the curricular overlap between the two programs.
